mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt B14XER engine for a Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo typically costs £1,000-£1,600 supply-only or £1,400-£2,500 fitted. Used units start from £300, and reconditioned options sit between £700-£1,200. A14XER variants are similar in cost - £1,000-£1,600. Timing chain replacement (if caught early) is £400-£650. All EnginesMarket quotes include 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain stretch on a Meriva 1.4 Turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign of timing chain stretch is a rattling noise on cold start - typically lasting 1-2 seconds before the oil pressure builds. Other signs include a check engine light, reduced performance, and in severe cases, a non-starting engine. The B14XER timing chain tensioner can wear prematurely. If you hear a rattle on start-up, get it inspected immediately. A snapped timing chain on this interference engine causes catastrophic damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2010-2015 Meriva B 1.4 Turbo worth £1,500-£4,000, a £1,400-£2,500 engine replacement is borderline unless the vehicle is in exceptional condition with low mileage. For vehicles worth over £2,500, replacement is typically viable if the rest of the car is sound. The 1.4 Turbo is a reliable engine when timing chain maintenance is kept up. Compare the cost of a rebuilt unit with warranty vs. buying another used Meriva. We always recommend a specialist inspection before any decision.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B14XER and A14XER are generally reliable when properly maintained. Timing chain stretch is the most common issue (typically 60k-100k miles), but with preventative maintenance - including regular oil changes and timing chain inspections - many 1.4 Turbo engines exceed 120,000 miles without major failure. The 1.4 Turbo is one of the better petrol options in the Meriva range. Coil pack failure is common but cheap to fix (£70-£100 per coil). Regular oil changes using the correct GM-spec oil are essential.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement on a Meriva 1.4 Turbo typically takes 2-3 working days for a specialist (3-5 days for a main dealer). Timing chain replacement is 1-2 days. Coil pack replacement is a 1-hour job. Turbocharger replacement is 1-2 days. Supply & fit providers may offer courtesy vehicle options.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the B14XER and A14XER?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B14XER is the original 1.4 Turbo engine fitted to the Meriva B from 2010, producing 118hp. The A14XER is a later variant from around 2013 with slightly different emissions calibration, also producing 118hp. Both engines are essentially identical in terms of power and specification. The A14XER may have minor differences in ECU software. When replacing, ensure the replacement engine matches your vehicle's specific ECU calibration.

historyTimeline.h2: Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Petrol Turbo - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 1.4 Turbo petrol engine was introduced to the Vauxhall Meriva range with the second-generation Meriva B in 2010. Part of GM's Family 0 engine family, the turbocharged 1.4 offered a compelling blend of performance and economy for family MPV buyers who wanted more punch than the naturally aspirated 1.4 Twinport but better fuel consumption than the 1.8 petrol. The engine remained available through the Meriva B's production run until 2017.

milestones.description: Meriva B launched; B14XER 1.4 Turbo introduced at launch
B14XER continues with minor emissions tuning
A14XER variant offered in some markets; largely identical
Meriva B production ends; 1.4 Turbo discontinued

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 petrol turbo is covered below, with UK used and rebuilt pricing and known failure points - including timing chain stretch issues, coil pack failures, and turbocharger oil feed concerns.

commonProblems.h2: Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Petrol Turbo Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 1.4 Turbo (B14XER/A14XER) is a popular, efficient engine - but it has predictable failure points as it ages. Timing chain stretch is the most common issue, followed by coil pack failures and turbocharger oil feed problems. Rebuilt 1.4 Turbo engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing components and new turbo oil feed lines, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo Develops Startup Rattle
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can wear prematurely, leading to chain slack. This causes a characteristic rattle on cold start. If left unaddressed, the chain can skip teeth or break, causing catastrophic valve and piston damage. [THIRD-PARTY]

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain, tensioner, guides, and camshaft sprocket replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early - rattle on start-up only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt B14XER with new timing components and turbo
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has snapped or caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2015 Vauxhall Meriva B 1.4 Turbo is worth £1,500-£4,500 depending on year, mileage, and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. Timing chain replacement (£400-£650) is well within value for any running example. A full engine replacement (£1,400-£2,500) is viable for vehicles worth £2,500+, but for sub-£2,000 examples, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: Timing chain stretch is the single most important issue to address on the 1.4 Turbo. If you hear a rattle on cold start, get it inspected immediately - a £400-£650 repair is far cheaper than a £1,400+ engine replacement. We recommend a timing chain inspection at 60,000 miles as preventative maintenance.

problems.h4: Coil Pack Failure - Misfires and Loss of Power on the Meriva 1.4 Turbo
problems.rootCause: The coil packs on the 1.4 Turbo can fail, causing misfires, a flashing engine management light, and a noticeable loss of power. This is a common issue across GM's Family 0 engines. [THIRD-PARTY]

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Single coil pack replacement, spark plug check
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: All four coil packs and spark plugs replaced

repairOptions.longevity: Only if coil failure has caused other engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Coil pack replacement (£70-£100 per coil) is inexpensive and well within value for any Meriva 1.4 Turbo.
problems.recommendation: Coil pack failure is a relatively cheap and straightforward fix. If you experience a misfire, we recommend replacing the faulty coil pack immediately - and consider replacing all four if the car has over 60,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B14XER Vauxhall Meriva 1.4 Turbo engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Oil Feed Blockage - Turbo Failure on the Meriva 1.4 Turbo
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger oil feed pipe can become partially blocked with sludge, starving the turbo of oil and leading to bearing failure. Symptoms include blue smoke from the exhaust, a whistling noise from the turbo, and loss of power. [THIRD-PARTY]

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo core rebuild with new bearings and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; oil feed pipe must be cleaned or replaced

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or reconditioned turbocharger with new oil feed pipe
Complete rebuilt B14XER with new turbo and oil feed
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Turbocharger replacement (£800-£1,400) is viable on any Meriva 1.4 Turbo worth £2,000+. For sub-£2,000 examples, evaluate whether a used turbo (£200-£400) plus fitting is more cost-effective.
problems.recommendation: Regular oil changes using the correct grade and specification are essential to preventing oil feed blockage. If you experience turbo symptoms, have the oil feed pipe inspected before replacing the turbo - fitting a new turbo to a blocked oil feed will destroy it.
